transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because flying has gotten... really hard. Just the thought of getting on an airplane scares me so badly. I know, logically, it doesn’t make sense, but my body reacts like that plane is going to fall.
Is this fear only about flying, or do you get the same kind of fear in other situations too?
It’s really just flying. The fear hits when I think about getting on an airplane—like I know it doesn’t make sense, but I feel like the plane is going to fall.
When you think about flying or get on a plane, do you suddenly have a panic attack?

Yes. It can happen really fast. Even just getting an email about a rural shift where I’d have to fly—my heart starts pounding right away, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close the message.
Do these panic attacks ever happen out of the blue when you’re not thinking about flying or near an airplane?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed them coming out of nowhere—it's usually tied to flying or something that reminds me I’ll have to fly.
Aside from flying, are there any other situations you avoid because you’re afraid you might panic or not be able to escape?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not avoiding other places because of panic or feeling trapped. It’s really centered on flying.
